ABSTRACT

DIVERSITY AND SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF MACROALGAE IN THE SEMBILAN ARCHIPELAGO, MALAYSIA

Journal: Environment & Ecosystem Science (EES)

Author:Mohamad Saupi Ismail, Nur Farah Ain Zainee, Mohammad Rozaimi Jamaludin, Md. Nizam Ismail, Mei Ling Khoo, Su Nyun Pau Suriyant i, Chee Kong Yap

This is an open access article distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution License CC BY 4.0, which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original work is properly cited

DOI: 10.26480/ees.02.2026.113.120

This study evaluates the diversity and spatial distribution of macroalgae in the Sembilan Archipelago, Perak, Malaysia, with particular emphasis on crustose coralline algae and their ecological significance in coral reef systems. Field surveys were conducted between September and October 2020 across seven isles using line transect-quadrat sampling and sediment trap analysis. A total of seven macroalgal taxa were identified, comprising four filamentous species (Bryopsis pennata, Centroceras clavulatum, Lyngbya majuscula, and Zygnema sp.) and three crustose taxa (Lithophyllum sp., Mesophyllum sp., and Ralfsia sp.). Among these, Lithophyllum sp. exhibited clear dominance across multiple sites. Marked spatial variation in macroalgal coverage was observed, with Pulau Saga recording the highest abundance, whereas Pulau Rumbia displayed minimal coverage. Sedimentation rate emerged as a key environmental driver, with reduced sediment input corresponding to increased crustose algal dominance. However, deviations from this pattern suggest that additional factors, including water clarity and substrate characteristics, contribute to shaping community structure. The findings underscore the functional importance of crustose macroalgae in reef stabilisation, carbonate production, and habitat formation. This study provides critical baseline data for the Sembilan Archipelago. It emphasizes the need for continued monitoring to support ecosystem-based management and conservation strategies in Malaysian coastal waters, particularly within the Strait of Malacca.
